nodes.title: Director re-run after the structural block S1-S5 (director3, 357cc407): 12 lessons (c4/c5/c6 × 4 scenarios), ~$0.21, screen recorded per turn. Three Claude judges, one per class, every turn against director2; not blind. Fixed: costume labels, picture→real board and game, card closed after 2 misses, Hindi acknowledged, recitals mostly gone, arithmetic. Not fixed (the owner's core): answer inside the question (c4 ~9 per run), ignored answers in every class, worked examples one step and no 'toh jawab' (never in c4: gap at step 0), no class-level practice (c6's only item is '3 × 160'), unkept promises (cricket, Golu), speech disconnected from screen (the guard strips board references), rate-as-fraction in c5. ~0.5 s slower. docs/design/round7/judgements/director3-2026-11-05.md.

Replace per-turn improvisation with authored, verified lesson scripts per skill (hook, explain beats with board refs, a full worked example, keyed checks targeting misconceptions, a class-level practice ladder, class-level remediation, bridges), authored in-session by Claude agents and blind-verified by a separate Claude solver (no Azure). The Director walks the script; the reply model only paraphrases the beat and first answers the child's last turn. A listening contract (respond-first by turn type, always correct wrong answers, return parked promises before the wrap) and a screen contract (the reply sees and refers to what is up) are enforced in code. Pilot on the 3 judged topics, then director4. Why: dc-r7-brain-structural-block's reversal triggered (jd-r7-director3-2026-11-05). Reverse: director4 on scripted topics still shows the gaps (then the reply layer: stronger model on paraphrase only, or a code-rendered teaching voice).

md.measurements:
## jd-r7-director3-2026-11-05 (main loop judge, 2026-11-05)

Method: stream A's harness at 357cc407 (integration 5 + S1-S5 + Learning 008 + App 008 + the boardItemOf fix), results/2026-11-05-director3, against results/2026-11-04-director2. n = 12 lessons (c4/c5/c6 × steady/offtopic/stuck/steering), the same scripted Hinglish child, `screen` recorded per turn. Three Claude judges (one per class) read every teacher turn; the main loop combined their findings; not blind. Details and quotes: docs/design/round7/judgements/director3-2026-11-05.md.
md.decisions:
## dc-r7-teaching-scripts (2026-11-05, main loop)

Three fix rounds (11 items, then structural S1-S6) made her more truthful but did not make her teach. The core gaps persisted: the answer inside the question, ignored answers, no complete worked example, no class-level practice, unkept promises, speech disconnected from the screen. That is dc-r7-brain-structural-block's reversal condition. The diagnosis is that per-turn improvisation with guards cannot produce a coherent lesson. The teaching becomes authored data: lesson scripts per skill, written and blind-verified in-session by Claude agents (precedent: the 18 end-of-class items and the relevel ratings; no Azure calls). The Director walks the script; the reply model paraphrases and must first answer the child. Listening and screen contracts are enforced in code. Pilot: the three judged topics. Reversal: if director4 on scripted topics still shows the gaps, the reply layer is the next suspect.
